items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And two other guys were Barney, I mean Bobby Troup — I didn’t know this — and Ray Anthony, both up for the job.

ctx.x: How did you get to know him?

Well I got to know him, he was a fan of mine. [pause for refreshment] That’s right keep bringing ‘em in. Stop putting all that vodka in this. I quit drinking years ago. I thank you very much. He was a fan of mine. He used to come, in New York, when I played Birdland. He’d come in all the time to hear me. And when I moved out to California he’d come in to see me playing all the time. And I moved back to New York for almost a year and I got called, he was doing a television show and I got called — he quit the show…

a question, “yes,” “no,” he asked him. Finally I said, “Regis, I want to ask Basie a question.” He said, “Go ahead, Terry.” I went down and said, “Basie, when we played in Detroit that time, remember that scene with Pee Wee Marquette? Tell Regis.” He had to tell the story now. So every time we had a jazz musician — Stan Getz, every time he interviewed, I had to be down there with him. He was really great. That wasn’t his bag. I used to put him on all the time. He always thought that we were putting him on because…
